Biodiversity  
 
Biodiversity Action Plan 2025 – 2030: The Draft Biodiversity Action Plan 2025 - 2030 public consultation 
closed on 10 November 2025. Submissions received are under review for updating the Plan, Assessments 
and Report in preparation for Plenary meeting to adopt the Plan.  
All Ireland Pollinator Plan: Completed and submitted Leitrim County Council’s annual report to 
National Biodiversity Data Centre as a Council partner.  
Local Biodiversity Action Fund: Funding recoupment has been submitted to NPWS for biodiversity 
projects which were completed in 2025 
Heritage Council: Local Biodiversity Action Plan funding recoupment has been submitted to the 
Heritage Council for actions related to the development of the Biodiversity Action Plan.  
 
COMMUNITY AND INTEGRATION 
 
Local Enhancement Programme 2025 
On 13th June 2025, the Department of Rural and Community Development and an Gaeltacht announced 
€114,782.86 for 148 projects in Co Leitrim under the Local Enhancement Programme 2025. All payments 
have been made under the Current and Capital stream and redistribution of funds has been approved 
and paid out. 
 
Age Friendly Programme   
Briefing session with businesses completed in Mohill in relation to delivering Age Friendly and Dementia 
training. Recruitment for delivery of the programme is underway in both Carrick on Shannon and Mohill 
with programme delivery scheduled for the end of January 2026. 
LEO updated the details of all businesses currently recognised as Age Friendly in Mohill. 
Age Friendly content was prepared and included in the ‘Stay Safe Stay Well’ winter ready events. 
Healthy Ireland 
Healthy Leitrim in conjunction with EduFit delivered an online programme ‘MenoWell’ to over 180 
participants in Leitrim. This course is an online evidence-based exercise, nutrition, and health education 
programme promoting wellness for women in all stages of adult life. Theses educational pieces were 
delivered through our Period Dignity programme funded through the Department of Health. We also 
delivered two workshops online for teenage girls focusing on menstrual health education, with the first 
workshop delivered to active girls, and the second aimed at more sedentary teenagers.

6 
 
Healthy Leitrim continues to collaborate with Age Friendly Ireland and the HSE Understand Together 
programme, with an information afternoon held in Mohill for local businesses on November 6th. Healthy 
Leitrim also continues to collaborate with Age Friendly Ireland on the pilot project within Leitrim nursing 
homes, with potential funding to be allocated to the project in 2026 for ‘Book of Life’ memory books to 
be run as a pilot project.  
 
On International Mens Day Healthy Leitrim collaborated with the Integration Team to deliver walking and 
talk café’s for mental health. These events took place in Ballinamore and Dromahair. 
 
Healthy Leitrim presented at the ‘Stay Safe, Stay Well This Winter’ roadshows in Ballinamore and Mohill 
in collaboration with Leitrim Fire Services, Leitrim Community Policing Unit, and Leitrim Community 
Safety Partnership. 
 
Healthy Leitrim collaborated with Peace Plus on the very successful delivery of three events. A caring for 
the carers event took place in Manorhamilton with a strong attendance, and two events targeting people 
living in severe isolation – specifically older adults in Ballinamore, and men in North Leitrim of no fixed 
abode or living in total isolation. From the isolation events 5 people were referred on to their GP for 
further health checks. 
 
Healthy Leitrim attended Leitrim PPNs plenary in North Leitrim on November 13th. 
 
Community Recognition Fund 
Leitrim has been allocated over €2.2 million under this funding programme, which will be invested 
across 16 capital projects throughout the county. The Community Development and Integration team 
continues to support the grantees in the roll out of their capital projects.  
 
PEACEPLUS 
 
Leitrim PEACEPLUS Action Plan (1.1) 
 
Local Community Regeneration & Transformation 
• We are finalising tender packages for Play & Art Therapy Facility in Drumkeeran and the MUGA in 
Ballinamore.  
• Construction tenders assessed for Coleman’s (Carrick Youth Arts & Community Space) Sean 
Quigley has been appointed to carry out the refurbishment works 
 
Thriving & Peaceful Communities  
• The Community Biodiversity Programme was promoted at the Love Where You Live Awards where 
an information leaflet was circulated to over 200 members of Leitrim’s community & voluntary 
network. 
• The first of our Digital Camps for young people was held in The Junction in Ballinamore over the 
October mid-term. Over 60 young people attend a day long camp which included digital 
awareness, VR & coding and digital art. 
• Applications for the QQI Level 7 in Community Work (Special Purpose Award) were opened up 
with the deadline for submissions the 8th December. 
 
Celebrating Cultural Diversity

7 
 
• Ballinamore Area Community Council have been appointed to deliver a Practical Skills Training 
Programme which will include tractor skills, first aid, quad bike certification among others. It will 
be delivered in locations around the county. 
 
PEACEPLUS Shannonside Peace Arena Timeframes (1.4) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Management 
• 
Crowleys DFK have been formally appointed as Auditors (Controllers) and will be certifying all 
financial claims and expenditure under both PEACEPLUS programmes 1.1 & 1.4  
 
Local Community Safety Partnership (LCSP) 
The Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, has commenced. Regulations have been received 
which will provide a framework for establishing the Local Community Safety Partnership in line with the 
provisions of the Act.  
In accordance with the legislation the membership of the LCSP will be community focused. Statutory 
services including AGS, HSE, TUSLA and seven local Councillors will be mandated onto the LCSP. Local 
Members have been recruited to represent local residents groups & minority groups via the PPN, Rural 
interests, Victims of Crime, Older Persons, Sports & Business Reps are also being recruited and have been 
submitted to the National Office of Community Safety (NOCS) for approval by Minister O’ Callaghan. 
Induction of LCSP partnership members will take place on receipt of Ministerial approval of members 
with first meeting due to take place in January.  
Financial claim has been submitted to NOCS for salary recoupment and €10,000 partnership set up cost. 
Issues paper submitted to NOCS for Leitrim to inform development of National Community Safety 
Strategy.  
LCSP coordinator has commenced in Post in November.   
 
Local Authority Integration Team (LAIT) 
• In November, the Integration Team conducted 10 clinics aimed at identifying the needs of 
residents and families. Three clinics focused on Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection (BOTP) and 
the 7remaining focused on International Protection Accommodation Centres in Leitrim. 
• One ‘Offer a Home’ activation was successfully completed in November, providing 
accommodation for two families units accommodating 5 individuals in total.

8 
 
•  The Integration Team partnered with Tusla Child and Family agency to carry out a consultation 
with Parents residing in Dromahair to ascertain the needs and challenges when parenting in 
Ireland a total of 15 parents were in attendance 
• Children not currently availing of the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) Scheme –have 
received Play Pack funded nationally through County Childcare Committee’s. Children In Abbey 
Manor and Carraig Accommodation received packs 
• Young People aged 12–17: “Finding the Balance” – This initiative explored themes such as 
culture, diversity, and integration. The programme supported 7 young people in navigating their 
new environment, flourishing within it, and actively engaging with their peers and the wider 
community. This programme was funded through the Children and Young People Service 
Committee – Healthy Ireland Fund. 
• The Integration Team held a Community and Integration Christmas Event in November in the 
Island Theatre, Ballinamore. This event was attended by families residing at Abbey Manor Hotel, 
Dromahair, Carraig Accommodation Centre, Ballinamore, Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection 
and families from the community. A total of 98 people attended the event where they took part in 
Christmas t-shirt printing, face painting and a disco.

ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, REGENERATION, SUSTAINABLE 
TRANSPORT & EMERGENCY SERVICES 
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT 
STEM Passport for Inclusion- Maynooth University & ATU 
3 Secondary Schools, Lough Allen College, Drumshanbo Vocational School and Mohill Community 
college had the first one day workshop of STEM Passport for Inclusion programme (level 6 award) during 
the month of November. Carrgallen Vocational School will commence in January 2026. 
A number of National Schools around the County have signed up to take part in the Microsoft 
Dreamspace Programme 2025/2026. 
 
Broadband Connection Points – Upgrade of BCP equipment.   
The upgrade of the BCP equipment for the 12 BCP sites is almost complete with one to be finalised. 
 
Carrick on Shannon Business Campus 
Building on the completed feasibility study for a proposed Enterprise Hub at Carrick on Shannon 
Business Campus, work advanced on planning for a tender for consultancy services to develop a suite of 
work packages to move the project from concept validation to implementation readiness, through the 
development of a comprehensive business, design and governance framework.  The tender was 
published on the eTenders platform on 31st October, and the closing date has been extended to 15th 
December 2025. 
 
County Promotion 
The Intercounty Promotion Event on Nov 27th at the Irish Embassy in London was well received with very 
positive feedback and over 100 attendees on the evening.  
The breakfast meeting with Leitrim Diaspora in London on Nov 28th went well with those in attendance 
keen to support future initiatives.  
 
Leitrim Diaspora 
Works continues the development of the framework for the Leitrim Diaspora Strategy, 2026-2030.  
Meetings of the Diaspora Working Group and Steering Groups took place in November, further meetings 
are planned for Q1, 2026. 
   
Leitrim Economic Forum and Global Business Network 
There were no meetings of the above groups in November, the next meetings of the groups are on the 5th 
and 10th December, respectively.   
Work is ongoing on the procurement of a consultant to deliver a new Economic and Skills Strategy for 
county Leitrim.  Discussions are taking place on planning A Leitrim Business Summit for 2026, both of 
these initiatives will be part of the Economic Forum Work programme. 
 
DRCD Funded Schemes 
ORIS Measure 2 & 3 funding was announced, and of the 63 projects nationally, Leitrim has received 
funding for one project, the construction of a 1.95km greyway between Dromod and Roosky, along the 
L1601, which was approved €500,000.  
The CLÁR funding announcements were made during November, a total of 206 approvals were made 
throughout the country, with Leitrim receiving approval on nine projects, totalling €537,118.

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE (LEO) 
 
Training, Mentoring & Export      
A large number of people received training in November as we ran a series of courses such as Small 
Business Accounts training; Canva Advanced Design Techniques; Small Business Accounts for 
Childminders; Workshop for Limited Company Directors; MicroFinance Ireland Loans Information Session; 
an in person Start Your Own Business Course and a 1:1 Marketing Review Clinic. 
Demand for one-to-one mentoring continues to remain high. Assistance is also available on Export related 
issues and can be booked online free of charge to discuss any issues facing businesses or identifying and 
managing opportunities available for exporting.  
 
All In A Days Work Programmes & Associated Financial Supports

13 
 
The “All In A Days Work” campaign continues to be rolled out on the areas of Lean, Green and Digital 
supports.  There is significant growth in demand for all three supports, in particular the Energy Efficiency 
Grant (EEG) and Grow Digital (GD) Voucher.   The EEG, with up to 75% of eligible costs up to a maximum 
grant of €10,000 can be supported following the completion of a Green for Business, Green Start or a SEAI 
Energy Audit.   The GD voucher is a grant covering 50% of eligible costs (minimum grant of €500 up to a 
maximum grant of €5,000) limited to new software subscriptions for a period of 12 and training and 
configuration of the software. 
 
Atlantic Economic Corridor Update:  
Interreg Europe Digital Rural: Leitrim continues its partnership under Interreg Europe. The Digital Rural 
Project empowers rural communities through smart technologies and collaborative policymaking to 
foster sustainable regional development.  
 
PEACE Plus – DS3 Project 
The DS3 Project under PEACE Plus (Smart Towns & Villages) launches in November 2025, running until 
July 2028. It promotes cross-border collaboration through ICT in community services and economic 
activity. Leitrim County Council leads Work Package 2, with one contract awarded for a mobile fab lab 
and another tender currently live. Workshops are due to commence in the new year.  
 
Creative Heartlands 
Screen Ireland funding has been secured and a new programme of training and mentoring for the screen 
sector has been developed. The programme launched in October and will run until May 2026. This will 
cover Leitrim, Sligo, and Roscommon. Two events have already taken place under this programme, and 
a comprehensive mentorship programme will be established.  
 
Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan Implementation 
Northwest Vision Development 
The x3 Chief Executives from Leitrim/Sligo/Donegal are collaborating to develop a Northwest Region 
Vision which will feed into the REP development in 2025. There has been a number of working groups with 
hypotheses presented to the working group. Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director of 
Economic Development and the NW Programme Manager. In November the x3 Chief executives of Sligo 
Leitrim and Donegal met to review OCO’s progress and to provide guidance.  
 
Energy working group 
A multi-agency supported project is underway which will explore the opportunities available to the region 
with available unused energy from our renewable energy sources in the region e.g. onshore wind energy. 
Opportunities being explored are green energy parks, marketing, hydrogen etc. This package was kicked 
off in October. Leitrim CoCo is represented on the project by Director of Economic Development and the 
NW Programme Manager. 
 
10xNW 2026  
Following a very successful event in 2025, a collaborative course of multiple agencies in the Northwest 
region are coming together to host the 10xNW entrepreneurship exchange in February 2026 in Leitrim. The 
working group have convened and are planning this.  
 
Next REP development 
The Final report of the Northwest Regional Enterprise Plan 2022-2025 is currently in draft form and once 
approved by DETE will be published on DETE website. Currently DETE are undergoing a review of the REPs

14 
 
with the intention of taking recommendations from the review towards the next REP development which 
is due to kick off Q1 2026. 
 
 
TOURISM 
 
Influencer Marketing 
In November, Sara Kennedy from Irish Weddings visited four venues in County Leitrim: Drumhierny 
Woodland Hideaway, Lough Rynn Castle, The Old Rectory, and The Landmark Hotel. Each offers a 
distinctive setting for celebrations, showcasing the diversity and charm of Leitrim as a destination. Sara 
will be publishing reviews and features on these venues, highlighting Leitrim’s appeal as a unique 
location for couples planning their special day. 
 
Fáilte Ireland Seminar Part 1 & 2: Developing Outdoor Accommodation  
The webinar highlighted the growth of outdoor accommodation in Ireland, with discussions on market 
opportunities, planning challenges, and funding supports. The second phase of planning was 
emphasised as a critical step for successful development, covering issues such as environmental impact, 
traffic, and local policy. A case study from Drumhierny Woodland Hideaway provided practical insights 
into marketing strategies and the steps involved in creating a successful outdoor accommodation 
business. The session also underlined the importance of sustainability, accessibility, and added 
experiences to enhance visitor appeal. Overall, the webinars offered both strategic guidance and real-
world examples to inspire future projects in this sector. 
 
NPA 
The tourism team attended a workshop hosted by Interreg Europe that focused on potential Northern 
Periphery and Arctic (NPA) projects. The session provided valuable insights into upcoming funding 
priorities, thematic areas, and partnership opportunities. It also outlined the application process and 
key timelines, with the next open call scheduled for February 2026. The workshop offered an opportunity 
to network with stakeholders from across Europe and to explore collaborative ideas that could 
strengthen regional development and innovation. 
 
Festival & Event Grants 
Claims for festival and event grants are actively being processed. Promotional support for upcoming 
events continues, with efforts focused on increasing visibility and driving attendance. 
 
Social Media Engagement  
Throughout November, the Tourism Team maintained active engagement across Instagram, Facebook, 
and Twitter. This activity was supported by the county-wide photography competition hosted earlier in 
the year, with winning entries selected to feature in the Leitrim Calendar. The final calendar has now 
been printed. 
 
Acres Lake  
The Tourism Team is currently finalising the design and installation of signage for the new facility at 
Acres Lake. The signage will include clear directional markers, information boards, and accessibility 
features to ensure visitors can easily navigate the site. Branding elements will highlight Leitrim’s identity 
and promote the facility as part of the wider tourism offering. The final stage involves coordinating with 
contractors to ensure the signage is in place ahead of the official launch, with attention given to 
visibility, and consistency across all entry points and key areas of the lake.
